column11: lookup.py demand 'Vyvgart Hytrulo': CMS Part B 2024, $150,829,226 over 902 beneficiaries = $167,216
column12: Judgement on the comparator. Vyvgart Hytrulo (efgartigimod/hyaluronidase) is the only non-immunoglobulin biologic approved for CIDP in the US (June 2024) and the product a new CIDP biologic would be priced against. Case against: (1) CMS 2024 beneficiaries mix gMG and CIDP and include partial-year CIDP starts from a June 2024 launch, so $167,216 understates a full year (Part D 2024 was $191,644, Vyvgart IV Part B 2024 $231,053); (2) VITALIZE's comparator is IVIg itself, which the book carries no CIDP-labelled brand for (only Octagam, labelled for other uses), and chronic IVIg can cost less than an FcRn blocker. Riliprubart's route of administration in phase 3 was not confirmed in this research; Part B is assumed because the trial compares against infused IVIg. In EUR because the engine models a company in its reporting currency and converts to dollars only at the end: $167,216.00 at EUR/USD 1.141100 (ECB via fetchers/fx_ecb.py, 2026-09-23) is EUR 146,539.30

Taken from the pool's own source because Blein's 1,113/3,409 chronic share (Komodo, 81% of the cohort treated) applied to Gable's pool (53.9% treated) gives 25,159, which is more than every patient on any immunoglobulin in Gable's 2023 pool (21,538). 77,058 x 0.2643 = 20,367 patients. Case for lower: this counts any IVIG claim in the year, and chronic users (8 or more courses) were only 1,113 of 1,803 immunoglobulin users in Blein 2026 (PubMed 41696747), so 0.2643 x 0.6173 = 0.163 on a cross-source basis. Case for higher: adding subcutaneous immunoglobulin gives 21,538 / 77,058 = 0.2795, and an FDA label could read 'CIDP' broadly.
